subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add a public anti-herd scheduling contract for heartbeat and cron every schedules, and should it be deterministic phase/stagger, prime cadence, explicit fixed-time phase, or no new timing knob?
rationale: Current source already implements stable heartbeat phasing and cron-expression staggering, but the missing request requires public config, CLI, protocol, persisted schedule semantics, defaults, docs, and upgrade behavior that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Design One Scheduler Contract
options.body: Add one documented, compatibility-preserving anti-herd model across heartbeat and cron every with schema/protocol, CLI/docs, readback, and focused upgrade tests.

options.title: Limit To Cron Every Stagger
options.body: Extend the existing cron stagger model to every schedules and leave heartbeat's implicit stable phase as the heartbeat behavior for now.

options.title: Decline New Timing Knobs
options.body: Keep current fixed-interval semantics plus existing heartbeat phase and cron-expression staggering, and close this only after maintainers state prime or public phase controls are out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design One Scheduler Contract
recommendation.body: Add one documented, compatibility-preserving anti-herd model across heartbeat and cron every with schema/protocol, CLI/docs, readback, and focused upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent maintainer-visible evidence across cron stagger and scheduler-adjacent PRs that would shape the public cron side of this decision.
